name: Violet Hunt
bio: Violet Hunt, later a novelist, was the daughter of the landscape painter Alfred William Hunt and the novelist Margaret Raine Hunt, of Tor Villas, Campden Hill, where Wilde took tea with the family during his Salisbury Street years. In 1880-81 he paid her marked attention - 'the sweetest Violet in England I think her', he wrote to her mother in March 1880 - promised and sent her a poem, and thanked her directly in July 1881 for admiring his Poems. Her autobiography The Flurried Years (1926), quoted by the editors for her reminiscence of the young Wilde at Tor Villas, is the family memoir of the acquaintance.
bio_note:
Facts from the main-particulars footnote at Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000), p. 88 n. 4 (repo PDF 113, folio confirmed, read as page image 2026-08-03) and Wilde's letters at pp. 88-9, 93, 94 (to Mrs Alfred Hunt) and 114 (to Violet Hunt). Full passages and the marriage-proposal pointer in dossiers/EARLY-CIRCLE_dossier.md.

BORN-YEAR, CROSS-CHECK RESOLVED 2026-08-04. The 1866 above is the Letters editors' figure and was flagged here for checking against a modern reference work. It is confirmed: Sutherland, Stanford Companion to Victorian Fiction (1989), p. 314, read by Lovelle Cardoso, also gives 1866. en.wikipedia and Wikidata (Q1677011) give 1862, and en.wikipedia cites Sutherland - the work that contradicts it. Its own article explains why: the 1862 date is an emendation, adopted so that Hunt would be old enough to be engaged when Oscar Wilde is said to have proposed to her in Dublin in 1879. That is a date reasoned backwards from an anecdote in order to make the anecdote work, which is the inference this reference declines to make (see CONTRIBUTING, 'What gets rejected'). We keep the attested year and record the emendation rather than adopt it.

The tension is real and is not resolved by keeping 1866. Ellmann has them meeting in London 'when she was not yet seventeen' (see the source on hunt--wilde), which fits neither 1866 (she would be about thirteen when the letters begin in March 1880) nor 1862 (about eighteen). Ellmann also puts the meeting in London at the beginning of the 1880s, not Dublin in 1879, and our own verified letters are London from March 1880. So the Dublin story carries a place and a date that the fullest account of the acquaintance does not support, and it is that story the 1862 date exists to accommodate. Anyone revisiting this should run down the Dublin claim to its origin first; the birth year is downstream of it. LETTER COUNT ESTABLISHED 2026-08-06 from the volume's Index of Recipients (printed 1233): 'Hunt, Violet - 114'. ONE letter, on one folio. A regex sweep of this map had put it at ten; those nine others belong to her mother, who has her own index entry - 'Hunt, Mrs Alfred - 88, 93, 94, 101, 102, 108, 315'. Nothing in this node was wrong, but the correspondence is much smaller than a surname search suggests, and that is worth knowing before anyone goes hunting for it.
